name: CHROMEWORKS Filament Series Precision Arm
description:
The Chromeworks Filament Series replaces the full arm with a mirrorpolished chassis housing 22 independently actuated micro-servo tendons capable of sub-millimeter positional accuracy, rated to ±0.08mm under load. The neural integration suite uses Chromeworks' proprietary SilkLink feedback mesh, which translates sensory return data with enough fidelity that surgeons report being able to feel the tension differential between tissue types. The arm's external profile is deliberately understated — brushed surgical chrome with minimal panel lines, designed to read as professional rather than augmented.

The Filament is the preferred arm of Meridian 88's elite surgical community, high-end watchmakers in the Midspire artisan districts, and licensed demolitions technicians who need to manipulate micro-detonator assemblies without triggering them. It carries a quiet prestige among Tier 3-4 technical professionals — owning a Filament means your hands are your livelihood, and you invested accordingly.
installation_requirements: Full shoulder disarticulation, Chromeworks-certified neural integration clinic, SilkLink mesh calibration (72-hour inpatient)
rejection_risk: Low – SilkLink mesh uses adaptive bioelectric signaling to minimize immune response; documented rejection rate under 4%
maintenance: Quarterly servo calibration, annual SilkLink mesh diagnostic, proprietary Chromeworks lubricant only

side_effects: Hypersensitivity feedback overload when handling rough or unexpected textures without dampening mode active
Users report difficulty switching off fine-motor awareness, causing insomnia in early adaptation period
Occasional servo ghost-movement during REM sleep — minor but startling to partners
Long-term SilkLink users develop measurable reduction in gross-motor tolerance for imprecision
cultural_context: In Meridian 88's surgical community, a Filament arm is the quiet credential that speaks louder than any certification plaque. Among the Midspire watchmaker guilds, lending your Filament hand for inspection is considered an intimate act of professional trust — a custom that has generated considerable social ritual around the arm's ownership and display.

story_hooks: A renowned surgeon's Filament arm has been remotely bricked mid-operation — someone is sending a message, and the patient is still on the table
A stolen Filament unit is circulating in the Shelf, repurposed with non-standard firmware that lets it crack biometric locks with terrifying precision
A watchmaker's guild is commissioning a secret project that requires a Filament-armed technician to work on something that isn't a watch
